item.title: Chapter 1: Reversals and Crimes Against Sound
item.description:
The silence in the Ocular dragged long enough for the hum of the crystal relays to sound deafening.

G’raha’s hand remained suspended mid-gesture, his fingers half-curled against the azure air. Beneath the heavy shadow of the cowl, his jaw worked twice, searching in vain for the grand, velvet rhetoric he had spent decades refining.

“You…” His voice cracked, the ancient sovereign evaporating on the syllable before he hastily cleared his throat to force it back down. “I… forgive me. The calculations did not—”

item.title: Prologue: The Folly of Best Laid Plans
item.description:
The mud in the Ghimlyt Dark had the consistency of wet lard and smelled of spent ceruleum.

It was a miserable, indecisive kind of cold—the sort that didn’t have the decency to freeze the ground solid, just spit sleet into your collar until your leathers were sodden and your shins ached. Around the revetment, the trench timber shuddered under the rhythmic, concussive hammering of imperial magitek artillery half a malm north.

item.title: The Flame, the Sunlight, and the Storm
item.description:
The Flame, the Sunlight, and the Storm

“Shut up,” she said, her rough Ala Mhigan contralto cutting right through his grand address. “I know it’s you under that stupid hood, G’raha Tia.”

The silence that followed was absolute. And as thick as a thousand-year-old tree.

I can’t be the only person whose immediate reaction to the Crystal Exarch opening his mouth was, “Oh, I know exactly who you are.”

The silence in the Ocular dragged long enough for the hum of the crystal relays to sound deafening.

G’raha’s hand remained suspended mid-gesture, his fingers half-curled against the azure air. Beneath the heavy shadow of the cowl, his jaw worked twice, searching in vain for the grand, velvet rhetoric he had spent decades refining.

“You…” His voice cracked, the ancient sovereign evaporating on the syllable before he hastily cleared his throat to force it back down. “I… forgive me. The calculations did not—”

“Shut up,” she said, her rough Ala Mhigan contralto cutting right through his grand address. “I know it’s you under that stupid hood, G’raha Tia.”

The silence that followed was absolute. And as thick as a thousand-year-old tree.

I can’t be the only person whose immediate reaction to the Crystal Exarch opening his mouth was, “Oh, I know exactly who you are.”

Vex crosses the rift straight out of the bloody trench-mud of Ghimlyt expecting an imperial ambush or an early grave. What she gets instead is a dying world drowned in blinding light, missing comrades, and an archivist playing savior in a dramatic bathrobe. She has three pounds of lead in her soles, a mouthful of fangs, and zero patience for a century-old martyr complex dressed up as civic duty. But saving Norvrandt means reckoning with what eighty-odd years did to him—and the feelings she buried when the iron doors of the Syrcus Tower first slammed shut.
